pages.title: Best streaming service for sports
pages.question: What is the best streaming service for sports?
pages.answer: For the most sports in one place, YouTube TV ($82.99) or Fubo (Pro $88.99) are the strongest picks because they carry local networks plus ESPN. On a budget, pair Sling Orange ($45.99) with Peacock ($12.99) or Paramount+ ($8.99) for specific leagues.

picks.why: Local ABC, CBS, FOX and NBC plus ESPN in one plan, unlimited DVR, and the only live service with NFL Sunday Ticket as an add-on.
Sports-first lineup, with regional sports networks in some markets.
The cheapest way to get ESPN channels in a live package (Orange, $45.99).
Sunday Night Football and NBA games on the $12.99 Premium plan.
NFL on CBS and UEFA Champions League from $8.99.
Thursday Night Football and NBA games, included with Amazon Prime.

pages.notes: Sports rights move often. Check each league's official broadcast schedule before you subscribe for a specific team.

pages.title: Best streaming service for kids
pages.question: What is the best streaming service for kids and families?
pages.answer: Disney+ is the best fit for most families because of its Disney, Pixar and Marvel library. The Disney+, Hulu bundle at $12.99 a month with ads adds shows for adults for 50 cents more than Disney+ alone.

picks.why: The largest family catalog among the major services.
Kids profiles with maturity controls and many animated originals.
Nickelodeon shows from $8.99.
DreamWorks and Universal family films on Premium.

pages.notes: Every service listed offers profile-level parental controls. Set them up on each device your kids use.

pages.title: Cheapest streaming services
pages.question: What is the cheapest streaming service?
pages.answer: The cheapest major paid plans are Netflix Standard with ads, Peacock Select, Paramount+ Essential and Prime Video standalone, all at $8.99 a month. The cheapest ad-free plan among the big services is Paramount+ Premium at $13.99.

picks.why: $8.99 with ads, $13.99 mostly ad-free: the lowest ad-free price in our list.
$8.99 with ads for the largest original library.
$8.99 Select for NBC and Bravo shows only.
Included if you already have Prime; $8.99 standalone.
$10.99 with ads, with annual billing to cut the cost further.

pages.notes: Rotating services (subscribe for a month, cancel, switch) usually saves more than any single cheap plan.

pages.title: Best live TV streaming service
pages.question: What is the best live TV streaming service to replace cable?
pages.answer: YouTube TV is the best all-around cable replacement at $82.99 a month: local networks in most markets, ESPN, 100+ channels and unlimited DVR. Sling TV ($45.99) and Philo ($25) are cheaper but leave out local channels.

picks.why: Most complete lineup with unlimited DVR.
Hulu + Live TV ($99.99) includes Hulu, Disney+ and ESPN Select.
Best for sports-heavy households.
Budget lineup with ESPN or a wide cable mix.
Lowest price for entertainment channels only.

pages.notes: Enter your ZIP code on each service's site before signing up. Local channels differ by market.
